Summary

Opening a PR no longer opens a separate window. The main window now shows the review queue in a sidebar and the selected PR's review beside it, so getting back to the queue doesn't mean moving windows around.

  • Opening: clicking a PR shows it. Return shows it and moves the keys to the review.
  • Back to the queue: ⌘0 or g p, from any window. It brings the main window forward, shows the sidebar if it was hidden, and focuses the list. Esc in the queue goes back to the review.
  • Switching is instant: reviews you've opened stay loaded, and one seen in the last minute isn't refetched. The diff scrolls back to where the cursor was.
  • Side by side: ⌥Return, or Open in New Window in the context menu, still opens a PR in a window of its own.
  • ⌘O: opens a PR by URL in the main window.
  • Marker: the sidebar marks the PR that's showing with an accent bar.

Stacked on #15, so merge that first.

Implementation notes

  • New file MainView.swift:

    • MainView is the window's root, a NavigationSplitView.
    • MainWindowState holds the open PR, the cached ReviewModel for each PR the window has shown, and requests to focus the queue.
    • MainWindows is a weak registry of main windows. It lets ⌘0 and Open Pull Request bring an existing main window forward instead of opening another.

  • ReviewQueueView became QueueSidebar. It's now just the list, the filter box and the toolbar buttons. MainView owns the selection, the filter and the focus, and handles the queue's keys.

  • ReviewView takes its model and no longer registers a key handler. KeyRouter keeps one handler per window, so MainView decides who gets each key:

    • the queue when the sidebar has focus or nothing is open;
    • the review otherwise.

    Clicking in the review takes focus off the list. ReviewWindow wraps a ReviewView for the separate windows. AGENTS.md records the one-handler-per-window rule.

  • Selection debounce. Selecting a PR waits 250 ms before showing it. Each review load is several gh calls, and arrowing through the list shouldn't load every PR it passes.

  • Scrolling back on return. DiffView's scroll-request task now also handles a .nearest request on its first run, so a reappearing diff scrolls to the cursor.

  • New command show-pull-requests (⌘0, g p), in GlobalCommands and the Window menu.

Testing

  • scripts/check: format lint, build and 70 tests pass. The keymap test now expects g p among the sequences a bare g would hide.
  • No new unit tests, because the change is all window and view wiring. The queue logic underneath is the tested MaserCore code from #15.
  • I couldn't screenshot the window: the terminal has no Screen Recording permission. Not checked by hand:
    • the sidebar's layout and width, and the open-PR marker;
    • click-to-show and its debounce;
    • Return moving the keys to the review, and j/k then moving the diff cursor rather than the queue;
    • ⌘0 and g p from the main window, from a separate review window, and with no main window open;
    • Esc from the queue back to the review;
    • ⌥Return opening a separate window;
    • ⌘O showing the PR in the main window;
    • going back to a PR keeping its tab, file and cursor;
    • launch URLs;
    • the Dock reopening a main window after it's closed.

Fixed a crash in f3d28d3 → 7bca94d: switching to the Files tab (g f) crashed, because the Files tab's own NavigationSplitView was nested inside the main window's. AppKit looped on constraint updates until it threw NSGenericException. The tab now uses an HSplitView. I reproduced the crash in a standalone app with the nested layout, and the same app ran clean with HSplitView.

Second fix in 4bb70cc. The Files tab still crashed in the main window. I bisected in the real app with a temporary hook that flipped tabs on its own: the constraint loop needs the resizable file tree and the comments inspector together. The tab is now three HSplitView panes (tree, diff, comments) and no longer uses an inspector, and it survived 16 tab switches with comments toggled on and off. Also: after a click in the sidebar, keys the queue doesn't use (c, g f, S…) now reach the open review instead of beeping.

More fixes from testing, in 8a5ac9e:

  • Pane widths: the file tree fits its widest row (160–360 pt), the comments pane is a fixed 320 pt, and the diff gets everything else. The queue sidebar defaults to 250 pt (at most 320).
  • c lost focus: on Overview it did nothing, and on Files the comment box lost focus to the queue list. The cause was .defaultFocus($focus, .list), confirmed by a scripted run in the real app with and without it.
  • Clicking a PR now hands the keys to the review. The queue gets them back only when clicked, or with ⌘0 / g p.

Key routing reworked in 8ec709c, from testing:

  • ⌘0 / g p now really gives the queue the keys. The window tracks who has them instead of trusting AppKit focus, which didn't move to the list.
  • / only filters while the queue has the keys. ⌘F still works from anywhere.
  • e shows and hides the queue.
  • Return / ⌥Return open the selected PR through the key router.

Each of these was checked with a scripted run in the real app.
